newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Petrobras must lose grip on Brazil alcohol - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras must lose grip on Brazil alcohol - analyst.

text.p: Brazil must remove control of its alcohol sector from state oil company Petrobras if it is to sustain and encourage domestic production of alcohol, said Jaime Rotstein, head of engineering consulting firm Sondotecnica.
"We need to establish new bases for the alcohol programme -- everything is always conditional on the position of Petrobras," Rotstein told a seminar on the future of the alcohol sector.
Brazil in May liberalized the anhydrous sector, meaning that Petrobras will cease to be the sole distributor of anhydrous alcohol at officially-set prices.
It plans to liberalize the rest of the sector, including sugar and hydrous alcohol, by May 1998.
Petrobras pays alcohol producers a price set by the government which includes subsidies and later sells the product at lower prices.
Earlier this year, the state oil monopoly halted payments to producers in the states of Sao Paulo and Pernambuco, saying it had cash-flow problems.

In the 1997/98 harvest, subsidies will total 1.7 billion reais ($1.58 billion), of which 1.4 billion will be destined to hydrous alcohol and 300 million reais to anhydrous alcohol, Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito told the seminar.

A key foundation of any future alcohol plan will be to "remove from Petrobras the possibility of intervention," said Rotstein, who has been studying Brazil's alcohol plan since its creation more than 20 years ago.

In addition, the government would have to restore the trust of the sector by showing it was committed to the continued production of alcohol, whose use as an alternative fuel for vehicles has been steadily decreasing since a peak in the 1980s.

The government will also have to take measures to penetrate foreign alcohol markets, including restoring talks with U.S. firms and establishing joint ventures with its partners in the Mercosur customs union, Rotstein said.
